- FE-AB1 (`d3bcb4a`): F-DG5-148 (record names wrap on Traceability and Modular entry) and F-DG5-149 (the Define Good-outcome table in a scroll region). FE-AB2 was stopped by a container restart; its partial work was kept as a WIP commit and its run as `*-orphaned`; the continuation FE-AB2B reviewed it, made no source change, re-recorded the before-fix failure and ran the acceptance checks (merge `45287b4`): the D-181 picker defect is fixed by a shared hook that follows `nextCursor`, used by the 12 picker screens.
- **Merged-tree verification of `45287b4`** (`orchestrator-D-182/verify-ab2-45287b4/`): `--historical --stage DG4`, install, typecheck, build, lint, format, openapi lint, contrast, unit (both locales) and integration exit 0; root e2e 32/32 and demo 10/10; web e2e **460/460 with C.UTF-8** and **459 passed, 1 failed with the locale unset**.
- **The one failure, disclosed:** `p5-launch-health-kpi.spec.ts:159` in chromium-ar: after Submit, `[data-assessment-status='submitted']` was not visible within the 5 s assertion timeout. Its trace was overwritten by the next run. A targeted re-run (`repro-health.log`: the picker spec then this spec, chromium-ar, `--repeat-each=5`) passed 20/20. **The cause is not established.** It is not counted as passed; the health-check screen uses the new all-pages picker, so qa is asked to examine it in round 7.
- **Round 7:** all three reviewers; qa verifies F-DG5-148 and F-DG5-149 and judges the D-181 fix and this failure. Then the release audit per D-140 option 1. | `docs/delivery/test-evidence/DG5/orchestrator-D-182/`. | — | 8:| D-181 | 2026-10-22 | delivery-orchestrator | **Wave AB's merged-tree verification found a pre-existing product defect: transformation pickers silently truncate.**
- Verification of `d3bcb4a`: static checks, unit (both locales), integration, root 32/32 and demo 10/10 exit 0; web e2e 456 passed and **2 failed** in each locale setting, the same two chromium-ar tests both times (`p5-procedure-outputs.spec.ts:39`, `p5-procedures-automation.spec.ts:256`): `selectOption(created.id)` on the launch-procedure transformation picker times out because the new transformation is not an option.
- **Cause:** `MyProceduresPage.tsx:204` loads `useTransformations({ sort: "code:asc", limit: 100 })`, one page, and offers only those. Wave AB's new spec adds transformations to the shared e2e database, so by the chromium-ar project there are more than 100 and the test's one is past the cap. The same single-page load (limit 50 or 100) feeds 12 other screens (`AssignmentsPage`, `RulesPage`, `RulePage`, `DelegationsPage`, `launch-plan/ui.tsx`, `AreaPages`, `DashboardsPage`, `BlockPage`, `reports/ui.tsx`, `MigrationsEntryPage`, `WalkthroughPage`). A user with more transformations than the cap cannot pick the others, and nothing says so. This is a product defect (REQ-S15 usability; no stale or partial data shown as complete), not test pollution; changing the test would hide it.
- **Decision:** fix it in the product in wave AB2, **T-DG5-FE-AB2** (frontend-ux-engineer): one shared hook that follows `nextCursor` to load every transformation the caller may see (the API's own page limit; no contract change), with a loading state and an error state, used by every picker that selects a transformation. A list that is deliberately a "recent" shortlist must say so in en and ar and offer the way to the full list. Unit tests for the hook (multi-page, error) and an e2e regression: with more than 100 transformations in the database, the launch-procedure picker offers the newest one, in en and ar. The two failing specs then pass unchanged.
- Then merged-tree verification again, round 7, and the audit per D-140 option 1. | `dg5/verify-AB/` logs, copied to `docs/delivery/test-evidence/DG5/orchestrator-D-181/`. | — |

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# qa-verifier: run a command against a DISPOSABLE PostgreSQL cluster (created, used and deleted inside this one
# process tree), exporting TEST_DATABASE_ADMIN_URL for the Vitest `integration` project (packages/db/test/global-setup).
#
#   tests/qa/support/with-pg.sh pnpm test:integration
#   tests/qa/support/with-pg.sh npx vitest run --project integration tests/qa/integration
#
# Environment: PGBIN (default: newest /usr/lib/postgresql/*/bin), QA_PG_PORT (default 24351: below the Linux ephemeral
# range 32768-60999, F-DG2-310). Port policy (tests/qa/support/pg-port.sh): QA_PG_PORT is the STARTING port; if
# postgres fails to bind (EADDRINUSE, e.g. a client socket in TIME_WAIT), it retries on a free port from MTH_PORT_POOL
# (default 25000-31999) up to MTH_PORT_RETRIES (10) times, logging each retry. QA_PG_STRICT_PORT=1 (or
# MTH_STRICT_PORT=1) makes a conflict BLOCKED instead. TEST_DATABASE_ADMIN_URL always carries the port actually used.
# No network is used. When run as uid 0 (build sandboxes), PostgreSQL runs in a user namespace as uid 1000 because it
# refuses to run as root. Missing binaries -> exit 3 and "BLOCKED" (never a silent pass).
# The cluster is ALWAYS UTF8 with the C locale (T-DG2-BE9), whatever the shell's LANG/LC_*: without them initdb
# would make a SQL_ASCII cluster, where char_length counts bytes. C (not C.UTF-8) because it exists on every platform
# and sorts by code point independent of the C library version.
set -euo pipefail

PGBIN="${PGBIN:-$(ls -d /usr/lib/postgresql/*/bin 2>/dev/null | sort -V | tail -1)}"

content.content:
## DOM-R6-13-decisions-d163-d168
Accepted as in rounds 4 and 5. Wave AA touches none of these areas, and this round's runs re-confirm them. D-163 (a): navigation is hidden server-side by grants. The office has 14 areas, including Administration for the Studio review; a technical administrator without transformation.read has 3. That is a sound reading of REQ-S03-007. D-164 (a)-(k): the #0071F1 navigation derives from the provisional #0078FF, and business-case totals are by reference. D-165: QA-F P-1/P-2/P-3, QA-E O-3 and QA-B O-1/O-2 affect neither RAG nor the value states nor approvals. The dev-mode demo binding works only on a dev-mode demo database (DOM-R6-11/12), and procedures v2 assigning baseline_validation.record_baseline to TL fits REQ-PB-027. D-166: Rule A (the intake adopts the transformation it produced) and Rule B (a finish-to-start forward pass over planned starts, never treating Unknown as 0 or overwriting approved plans) meet M0232's 'defined scheduling logic'; both are green in DOM-R6-09. D-167 is accepted. D-168: the B0147 lines are exact; only the chain-1 outcome wording point remains, which is acceptable.

## DOM-R6-14-requirement-acceptances
All 78 are met. REQ-S18-001's clause 'every demo screen, record and export shows the synthetic label in en and ar' now holds for the form-record export too (DOM-R6-02/03), as well as the report pipeline and the screens (DOM-R6-11). Its reset-determinism clause holds (DOM-R6-12). REQ-PB-089 ('every demo record and exported demo report') holds. REQ-S05-001's 'export returns the rows' holds with the label row added before the header in demo only. The other 75 are re-exercised as in round 5 by this round's source comparison, UI probes, 42-file integration batch, 30 root and 12 demo e2e tests. The disclosures remain acceptable, for example the REQ-S13-008 executive-pack staging gap and the REQ-S21-001 inbox label, as judged before. The notes of REQ-S18-001 and REQ-PB-089 still cite the pre-wave-AA runs and don't mention the form-record export. That is register drift with no behavioural effect, and it is not a finding.

## DOM-R6-15-environmental-residuals
The live registry (REQ-DLV-042 AC-1, D-057) and live CI (REQ-DLV-025 A24, D-058) are unreachable here; the offline install from the pinned lockfile and the build succeed (DOM-R6-00). Keycloak and a real demo IdP (D-049; ADR-0050 §1) are a devops item, and the D-165 dev-mode binding is the test path, which works (DOM-R6-11). No AI or external notification adapter ships in P5 (D-142 Q11), and A21 passes with the shipped 'disabled' configuration (DOM-R6-11).
